sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, password_hash, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique — POST /auth/login resolves the caller via findByEmail; must be a fast, exact lookup; employee_number: unique — duplicate detection on create; manager_id: MANAGER role scoping via findByManagerId (direct reports, one level)

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: role scoping (employeeIds = ANY(...)) and per-employee listing; status: status filter in findByQuery; (leave_type_code, start_date): leave-type + date-range filtering in findByQuery

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end): unique — findByKey enforces at-most-one-row-per-period; employee_id: GET /balances/me lists all balances for the caller

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_code, policy_name, annual_entitlement_days, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days, requires_manager_approval, effective_from, effective_to, status | pk: id | fks: leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: leave_type_code: findAll() is unfiltered and GET /balances/me filters by leaveTypeCode + effective window in service; an index supports the per-code selection

table leave_types | fields: code, name, requires_approval, max_consecutive_days, is_paid | pk: code | indexes: code: natural key — referenced by leave_policies.leave_type_code and leave_balances.leave_type_code

data_notes: Persistence changes for this feature are minimal and additive. The only schema change is a nullable `password_hash` column on `employees` (text contract, per the initial-schema convention of `t.text(...)` for text columns). All other tables already exist and are unchanged; their conceptual specs are recorded here for reference and to pin the index rationale the new read paths rely on. `LeaveRequestQueryParams` gains `employeeIds?: string[]` (matched via `employee_id = ANY($n)`) so role scoping stays in the query, not in application code. `IEmployeeRepository` gains `findByManagerId` for the MANAGER direct-reports scope. `IPolicyService` gains a method exposing the existing `IPolicyRepository.findAll()` (at-most-one ACTIVE policy per leaveTypeCode, latest effective_from wins) — no new repository method and no balance→leave-type dependency. Accrual-period helpers (`startOfUtcDay`, `addMonths`, `periodContaining`) are extracted to `src/shared/date/accrual.ts` and shared by LeaveService and the balance path. No new tables are introduced.
transaction_contract: This feature is read-only plus a single non-persistent write (POST /auth/login mints a JWT and returns a profile; it performs no multi-step DB writes). No transaction/unit-of-work contract is required. Read endpoints must not open a transaction.
